title: TuringSpace: Grounding Spatial Intelligence in Action with Interactive CAPTCHAs
why: Agents click and drag on a synthetic web CAPTCHA gym that trains and tests screenshot-based spatial actions.
mechanism: Changes evaluation and training: a programmatic web environment of 125 interactive spatial CAPTCHAs that must be solved by clicks and drags, used as both a benchmark and a training gym for screenshot-based MLLM agents.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported: humans 94.1% on the 125-task web gym; GPT-6 Astra fails 25.9% (74.1% success); Kimi K3 fails 68.0%; project page also reports at most 3.5% for CAPTCHA-trained GUI agents; Qwen3.5-9B fine-tuned on the gym rises from 1.6% to 33.1% and improves on seven OOD benchmarks, including a 9.9-point gain on VSI-Bench. Collector assigned no scores.

title: CANDID: Candidate-Driven Intervention for Disciplined Execution in Local Computer-Use Agents
why: Test-time intervention for local computer-use agents on OSWorld: filters looped actions and requires consensus before DONE.
mechanism: Changes the action/execution loop of local CUAs: at sparse failure-prone steps, parallel test-time candidates are filtered away from repeated behaviors, and termination requires unanimous DONE consensus rather than textual reflection.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported: experiments on OSWorld; structural control improves success rates over feedback-based alternatives with minimal execution overhead. Exact numeric results are not stated in the abstract. Collector assigned no scores.
